# **CHAPTER FOUR**

#  **SYSTEM DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION**

## **4.1 Objective of the New System**

The new system, named Praxis, is a web-based student union electronic voting platform created to replace the manual, paper-based conduct of tertiary institution elections. The central aim is to deliver a secure and verifiable channel through which eligible students register, authenticate, review candidate manifestos, and cast their ballots within a controlled time window.

The specific objectives that guided the design are stated below:

* To automate voter registration and institutional email verification so that only genuine students gain voting access.  
* To separate the content of a ballot from the identity of the voter, thereby guaranteeing ballot secrecy while still preventing repeat voting.  
* To compute results directly from an immutable vote ledger, removing human counting errors and shortening the interval between poll closure and result release.  
* To divide administrative authority into two tiers so that no single officer can unilaterally activate an election or publish an outcome.  
* To maintain a permanent audit record of every sensitive operation for accountability and dispute resolution.

## **4.2 Main Menu (Control Centre)**

The control center of Praxis is the persistent side navigation panel rendered on every authenticated page. It acts as the launch point from which a user reaches each functional area without returning to a home screen. The items presented adapt to the role attached to the signed-in account, so a student sees a lean list while a super administrator sees the full command set.

| Menu Item | Destination | Visible To |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Dashboard | Personal overview of active, upcoming and past elections | All roles |
| Admin Panel | Election creation and lifecycle control | Election Officer, Super Admin |
| Announcements | Publication of notices and reminders | Election Officer, Super Admin |
| User Management | Creation and removal of officer accounts | Super Admin only |
| Account Settings | Profile and password configuration | All roles |
| Notifications | Unread announcement indicator in the top bar | All roles |

## **4.3 Sub Menu / Sub System**

Each control center item opens a dedicated sub system that groups related tasks. The following breakdown shows how the platform is partitioned by responsibility.

| Sub System | Functions Provided |
| ----- | ----- |
| Authentication subsystem | Registration, email verification, sign-in, password reset, session handling. |
| Voter subsystem | Browsing elections, reading manifestos, comparing candidates, casting ballots, retrieving receipts. |
| Election management subsystem | Drafting elections, adding positions, scheduling, activation and closure. |
| Candidate management subsystem | Registering aspirants, editing records, and disqualifying with a logged reason. |
| Results subsystem | Tallying from the ledger, holding pending results, publication, and recount. |
| Governance subsystem | Officer account provisioning, eligibility configuration, and audit inspection. |

## **4.4 Database Specifications**

Persistent storage is handled by a relational SQLite database accessed through the Prisma object relational mapper. The schema is normalised to reduce redundancy, and a deliberate design decision keeps the cast ballot in a separate table from the voter record so that no query can link a person to a selection. The principal tables are specified below.

### **4.4.1 User Table**

| Field | Data Type | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| id | String (UUID) | Primary key, uniquely identifies each account. |
| fullName | String | Legal name of the registered user. |
| matricNumber | String, unique | Institutional matriculation or staff identifier. |
| email | String, unique | Institutional email used for verification and login. |
| password | String | Salted hash of the chosen password, never stored in plain form. |
| faculty | String | Faculty declared at registration. |
| department | String | Department of study. |
| level | String | Current academic level. |
| role | String | Access tier: STUDENT, ELECTION\_OFFICER or SUPER\_ADMIN. |
| isVerified | Boolean | Indicates whether the email has been confirmed. |
| createdAt | DateTime | Timestamp of account creation. |

### **4.4.2 Election Table**

| Field | Data Type | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| id | String (UUID) | Primary key of the election. |
| title | String | Official name of the election. |
| description | String | Summary of purpose and scope. |
| startTime | DateTime | Moment voting opens. |
| endTime | DateTime | Moment voting closes. |
| status | String | Lifecycle stage: DRAFT, SCHEDULED, ACTIVE, CLOSED or RESULTS\_PUBLISHED. |
| createdAt | DateTime | Record creation timestamp. |

### **4.4.3 Position and Candidate Tables**

| Field | Data Type | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Position.id | String (UUID) | Primary key of a contested seat. |
| Position.title | String | Name of the seat, for example President. |
| Position.electionId | String (FK) | Election the seat belongs to. |
| Candidate.id | String (UUID) | Primary key of an aspirant. |
| Candidate.fullName | String | Name of the aspirant. |
| Candidate.department | String | Department of the aspirant. |
| Candidate.level | String | Academic level of the aspirant. |
| Candidate.manifesto | String | Full statement of intent. |
| Candidate.slogan | String, optional | Short campaign phrase. |
| Candidate.isDisqualified | Boolean | Flags removal from the race. |
| Candidate.disqualifyReason | String, optional | Justification retained for audit. |
| Candidate.positionId | String (FK) | Seat being contested. |

### **4.4.4 Vote and VoterRecord Tables**

These two tables enforce ballot secrecy. The Vote table holds anonymous selections, while the VoterRecord table only confirms that a person participated. A composite unique constraint on the VoterRecord prevents any student from voting twice for the same seat.

| Field | Data Type | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Vote.id | String (UUID) | Primary key of an anonymous ballot. |
| Vote.electionId | String (FK) | Election the ballot belongs to. |
| Vote.positionId | String (FK) | Seat the ballot applies to. |
| Vote.candidateId | String (FK) | Chosen aspirant, with no reference to the voter. |
| Vote.castAt | DateTime | Time the ballot was recorded. |
| VoterRecord.id | String (UUID) | Primary key of a participation record. |
| VoterRecord.userId | String (FK) | Participating student. |
| VoterRecord.electionId | String (FK) | Election participated in. |
| VoterRecord.positionId | String (FK) | Seat participated in. |
| VoterRecord.receiptHash | String, unique | Cryptographic proof of submission returned to the voter. |
| VoterRecord.votedAt | DateTime | Time participation was logged. |

### **4.4.5 Supporting Tables**

| Table | Purpose |
| ----- | ----- |
| EligibilityRule | Stores optional faculty, department and level filters that gate participation per election. |
| Announcement | Holds notices linked optionally to a specific election. |
| AuditLog | Append-only record of actions, actor identity and timestamps. |
| VerificationToken | Time-limited tokens issued for email confirmation. |
| PasswordResetToken | Time-limited tokens issued for password recovery. |

## **4.5 Program Module Specification**

The codebase is organised into cohesive modules, each owning a controller on the server and one or more screens on the client. This separation keeps every concern independently testable.

| Module | Responsibility |
| ----- | ----- |
| Authentication module | Validates credentials, issues signed tokens, and manages verification and recovery flows. |
| Election module | Creates drafts, attaches positions, and transitions elections through their lifecycle. |
| Candidate module | Registers and maintains aspirant records, including disqualification handling. |
| Voting module | Accepts a selection, writes the anonymous ballot and the participation record atomically, and returns a receipt. |
| Results module | Aggregates ballots, determines winners, and controls publication and recount. |
| Announcement module | Publishes and retrieves notices for the dashboard. |
| Governance module | Provisions officer accounts, sets eligibility, and exposes audit entries. |

## **4.6 Input and Output Specification**

The tables below map the data supplied by users against the responses produced by the system.

### **4.6.1 Inputs**

| Input Form | Fields Captured |
| ----- | ----- |
| Registration | Full name, matric number, email, password, faculty, department, level. |
| Login | Email and password. |
| Election creation | Title, description, start time, end time, list of positions. |
| Candidate entry | Name, position, department, level, manifesto, slogan. |
| Ballot | One candidate selection per contested seat. |
| Officer creation | Name, email, password, department. |

## **4.9 Program Documentation and Implementation**

The application follows a client and server architecture. The browser client is a single page application built with the React library, while the server exposes a set of protected endpoints under a REST interface. Communication occurs over HTTP using JSON payloads, and every privileged request carries a signed token that the server validates before granting access.

On the server, an incoming request first passes through authentication middleware, then through role middleware that confirms the caller holds the required tier. The request then reaches its controller, which performs the operation through the data access layer and returns a structured response. On the client, each screen fetches its data on load and renders progressive feedback, so the user is never left uncertain about the state of an action. The build was verified after each feature by compiling the client bundle and starting both processes locally.

## **4.10 Language Justification**

JavaScript was adopted across the entire stack. This single language choice removes the friction of switching between two syntaxes and allows shared validation logic between the client and the server.

| Technology | Reason for Selection |
| ----- | ----- |
| React | Component-based rendering keeps the interface responsive and encourages reuse of visual elements. |
| Node.js with Express | Lightweight and event-driven, well-suited to handling many concurrent voting requests. |
| Prisma with SQLite | A typed data layer that guards against malformed queries and simplifies schema evolution. |
| JSON Web Tokens | Stateless session handling that scales without server-side session storage. |

## **4.11 Hardware and Operating System Requirements**

| Category | Minimum Requirement |
| ----- | ----- |
| Processor | Dual core processor rated at 2.0 GHz or higher. |
| Memory | 4 GB of RAM for development, 2 GB for a client device. |
| Storage | 500 MB of free space for the application and database file. |
| Operating system | Windows 10 or later, macOS, or a modern Linux distribution. |
| Runtime | Node.js version 18 or later installed on the host. |
| Client software | A current version of Chrome, Firefox, Edge or Safari. |
| Network | A stable internet connection for remote access to the server. |

## **4.12 Software Testing**

Testing was carried out at several levels to confirm that individual units behave correctly and that the assembled system meets its requirements. The table records representative test cases together with their expected and observed behaviour.

| Test Case | Expected Result | Observed Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Register with a non-institutional email | Request rejected with a domain error | Passed |
| Log in before email verification | Access withheld with a prompt to verify | Passed |
| Attempt to vote twice for one seat | Second attempt refused by the unique constraint | Passed |
| Officer tries to publish results | Action denied by the role guard | Passed |
| Change password with a wrong current value | Update rejected as incorrect | Passed |
| Cast a valid ballot | Receipt hash returned and confirmation shown | Passed |

Functional testing confirmed that every menu path leads to a working screen, while security testing confirmed that protected routes reject requests that lack a valid token or the correct role.

## **4.13 User Manual**

### **4.13.1 Guide for Students**

1. Open the platform and choose the option to create an account.  
2. Complete the form with accurate personal and academic details, then submit.  
3. Open the verification link sent to the supplied email address.  
4. Sign in and review the dashboard for elections that are open.  
5. Open an election, read the manifestos, and choose a preferred candidate for each seat.  
6. Submit the ballot and save the receipt returned by the system.  
7. Once results are released, revisit the election to view the outcome.

### **![][image7]**

![][image8]

### 

### **4.13.2 Guide for Administrators**

1. Sign in with an officer or super administrator account.  
2. Open the admin panel and create a new election with its positions and schedule.  
3. Register the aspirants for each seat through candidate management.  
4. Publish any relevant notices from the announcements area.  
5. When a super administrator is signed in, activate the election so that voting begins.  
6. After closure, publish the results and, if a dispute arises, trigger a recount.  
7. Provision additional officer accounts from the user management area as needed.
